# LoomSeal

> LoomSeal is the KordLoom proof format and its free, open verifier. A bundle is one JSON
> file carrying claims about what a system did, SHA-256 digests of the evidence behind them,
> their coordinates in an append-only hash chain, external anchors that fix that chain in
> time, and an ed25519 signature from the producer. Anyone can verify a bundle offline with
> the `loomseal` binary: no account, no server, and no trust in KordLoom or in the operator
> who sent the file. Two verifiers, one in Go and one written separately from the spec in
> Python, are cross-checked against the same conformance vectors, so the format is not held
> honest by a single implementation. The conformance wording is exactly four words: signed,
> chained, anchored, spanned. Apache-2.0.

Install: `go install github.com/kordloom/loomseal@latest`, then
`loomseal verify bundle.loomseal.json --evidence ./evidence`. Exit 0 verified, 1 verification
failed, 2 usage error.

## Pages

- [Home](https://loomseal.com/): a plain-language summary for non-engineers, why the format
  exists, a reproducible verification you can run in sixty seconds, and what a verified bundle
  does and does not prove.
- [The spec](https://loomseal.com/spec): the format itself. Bundle shape, canonical form
  (RFC 8785), producer keys and signatures, the three chain profiles
  (switchtender-audit-v1, loomseal-chain-v1), anchors, conformance
  levels, the verification procedure, and the claim-type registry.
- [LoomSpan](https://loomseal.com/span): the population attestation profile. Continuous
  signed counts on a fixed cadence turn silent omission into an affirmative lie. Coverage is
  reported as measurement, never as a badge.
- [FAQ](https://loomseal.com/faq): why it exists, the value to operators and to reviewers,
  the cryptography, how keys are kept, quantum computers, why not a blockchain, and what
  happens to your proof if KordLoom disappears.

## Reading

- [Tamper-evident logs, explained](https://loomseal.com/tamper-evident-logs): what
  tamper-evident means, how hash chains work, why anchoring is the missing half, how to
  prove a log was not altered, and what no log can prove.
- [IPE and the completeness problem](https://loomseal.com/ipe-completeness): what auditors
  mean by Information Produced by the Entity, why completeness is the expensive half, and
  what continuous population attestation changes.
- [Hash chains vs blockchains](https://loomseal.com/hash-chains-vs-blockchain): the shared
  core, what consensus adds and costs, and why anchoring answers what most projects
  actually need.
- [Verifiable evidence formats, compared](https://loomseal.com/evidence-formats): LoomSeal
  beside in-toto, SLSA, Sigstore, Certificate Transparency, RFC 3161, and WORM storage,
  honestly, including when the alternatives are the better choice.

## What it proves

A verified bundle proves the producer holding the signing key assembled those exact claims,
that the claims sit in an append-only order not reordered or rewritten since its heads were
anchored, and that supplied artifacts match their recorded digests. It does not prove the
producer observed the world honestly at capture time: a chain fixes the record, not the
character of the recorder. Keyed chains verify structurally for third parties and fully for
the key holder.

## Cryptography

SHA-256 for digests, HMAC-SHA256 for keyed chains, ed25519 for signatures. No blockchain, no
token, no consensus, no network dependency. Signature entries carry an algorithm field, so a
post-quantum signature algorithm can join ed25519 without a new envelope.

## Related

- [KordLoom](https://kordloom.com): the company. Software that proves itself.
- [SwitchTender](https://switchtender.com): runs a fleet from one binary, proves every change.
- [Source](https://github.com/kordloom/loomseal): spec, JSON schema, verifier, seal SDK for
  producers, and a signed example bundle anyone can verify.
